lessons.title: The: using al-
objectives: Add ال to a noun to say 'the'
Read definite nouns with correct vowels
starter: Say 'my book' and 'my bag' in Arabic.
Say 'this is a big house' in Arabic.
How do you ask 'whose is this?' in Arabic?

teach.heading: A book and the book
teach.note: Hold up one book and say 'a book'. Then point to the specific book and say 'the book'. Show how al- joins to the front of the word. Ask pupils where it is written: right side, the start of the word.

teach.heading: Dropping the -n sound
teach.note: Explain that with al- we remove the double mark of -un (tanween) and use a single mark. Do not discuss grammar terms; say 'two marks become one'. Pupils copy the change on mini whiteboards.

teach.heading: The ... is ...
teach.note: Contrast: بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ (a big house) vs الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ (the house is big). With al-, the sentence says 'the ... is ...'. Show the difference with colour coding. This is a key point and a common error.

teach.heading: Girl words with al-
teach.note: Use feminine examples. Pupils say each sentence and translate. Ask: why is it jameela not jameel? (hadeeqa is a girl word). Praise correct agreement.

teach.heading: Say it, spot it
teach.note: Flash words quickly; pupils say 'the' if it has al-. Then flash sentences and pupils translate. End by reading all sentences together.

practice: Say 'this is my bag' in Arabic.
Turn a book / a house / a mosque into 'the book / the house / the mosque'.
Say 'the garden is beautiful' in Arabic.
independent: Write 'the' forms of: بَاب / نَافِذَة / كُرْسِي / طَاوِلَة.
Write three 'the ... is ...' sentences with adjectives.
Draw a house and label with al-: الْبَابُ، النَّافِذَةُ، ...
exit: Say 'the mosque is big' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Write five sentences starting with 'al-' about things in your home.
lessons.send: SEND: highlight al- in colour, use sentence strips. EAL: compare with 'the' in home language. Stretch: write four sentences linking two nouns with wa (e.g. الْبَابُ كَبِيرٌ وَالنَّافِذَةُ صَغِيرَةٌ).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The weekend; Basem in the village; the little mouse and the lion
lessons.title: Bridge: the word al-; sun and moon letters
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do we sometimes not hear the 'l' in al-?
objectives: To understand how al- makes a word definite and how sun and moon letters change its sound
successCriteria: All: add ال (al-) to say 'the'
Most: sort words into sun letters and moon letters
Some: read sun letter words with shaddah correctly, e.g. الشَّمْس (ash-shams)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: reading the Qur'an correctly, where sun and moon letters are everywhere

keywords.def: sun letters: the l is silent
moon letters: the l is said

hook.text: Say 'the sun' in Arabic: الشَّمْس. Can you hear the ل (lam)? Now say القَمَر (the moon). What is different?
hook.a: In ash-shams the l is silent; in al-qamar we say it.

islamicLink.text: In Surah al-Fatihah we read الرَّحْمٰن (ar-Rahman) with a silent lam and الحَمْدُ (al-hamdu) with a clear lam. Knowing sun and moon letters helps us recite well.

starter.q: Bismillah. Plural of مُعَلِّمَة? A) مُعَلِّمَات B) مُعَلِّمُونَ

teach.heading: A book, the book
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. al- is joined to the front of the word. The tanwin (-un) drops when al- is added.

teach.heading: Moon letters
teach.note: The lam has a sukun: الْ. Pupils say al-qamar slowly.

teach.heading: Sun letters
bullets: The ل is silent; the next letter doubles
teach.note: Show the shaddah ّ on the letter after the lam. The 14 sun letters: ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن.

teach.heading: Sort the words
teach.note: Pupils show 1 or 2 fingers. Tip: if there is a shaddah after ال, it is a sun letter.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: س is a sun letter, so the lam is silent and the س doubles: as-sabt.

practice.model:
Add ال to the front: الشمس.
ش is a sun letter, so the ل is silent.
Put a shaddah on ش: الشَّمْس, ash-shams.

independent.q: Core: Add ال and write sun or moon: بَاب، سَيَّارَة، مَسْجِد، دَرْس، قَمَر، نُور.
independent.a: البَاب moon; السَّيَّارَة sun; المَسْجِد moon; الدَّرْس sun; القَمَر moon; النُّور sun
independent.model: Teacher does بَاب: البَاب. ب is a moon letter, so we say al-bab.

independent.q: Extend: Read aloud to your partner in a breakout room: الشَّمْس، القَمَر، الكِتَاب، السَّبْت.
independent.a: ash-shams, al-qamar, al-kitab, as-sabt

independent.q: Stretch: Find one sun letter word and one moon letter word in Surah al-Fatihah.
independent.a: For example: الرَّحْمٰن (sun), الحَمْدُ (moon)

exit.q: Which is a sun letter word? A) القَمَر B) الشَّمْس C) البَاب
Big question: why do we sometimes not hear the l in al-?
exit.a: Before a sun letter the l is silent and the next letter is doubled with a shaddah.

lessons.homework: Write five words with al- from your Qur'an reading and mark each one sun or moon.
lessons.send: SEND: sun and moon letter strips. EAL: picture of sun and moon with the two rules. Stretch: explain why الرَّحْمٰن has a shaddah on ر.

Portal arabic y4 lessons 1 and 2 (al- and sun and moon letters), combined for the bridge
Kitabi: definite and indefinite (CHECK IN KITABI)
Sun and moon letter sort cards (portal worksheet)
Mushaf or Qaidah for Surah al-Fatihah

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The weekend; Basem in the village; the little mouse and the lion
lessons.title: The weekend and the days of the week
lessons.bigQuestion: What do I do at the weekend, and how do I say the days in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name the days of the week and talk about the weekend
successCriteria: All: say the seven days in order
Most: say which days are the weekend: السَّبْت and الأَحَد
Some: say what I do: فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: days in a week and reading a calendar
lessons.smsc: Social: using the weekend to visit family and help at home

hook.text: In Britain the weekend is Saturday and Sunday. In some Arab countries it is Friday and Saturday. Why might that be?
hook.a: Friday is the day of Jumu'ah prayer, so some Muslim countries keep it as a day off.

islamicLink.text: Allah made Friday special with the Jumu'ah prayer (al-Jumu'ah 62:9). Many Arabic day names are numbers: al-ahad comes from 'one', al-ithnayn from 'two'.

starter.q: Bismillah. How do we read الشَّمْس? A) al-shams B) ash-shams
Is ق a sun letter or a moon letter?

teach.heading: The days of the week
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The Arabic week starts on Sunday. Spot the sun letters: ath-thulatha', as-sabt.

teach.heading: Days are numbers
teach.note: Help pupils remember: Sunday is day one, Monday day two, Tuesday day three.

teach.heading: The weekend
bullets: Today is: اليَوْمُ يَوْمُ الاِثْنَيْنِ (al-yawm yawm al-ithnayn)
teach.note: Pupils say today's day each lesson from now on.

teach.heading: What I do at the weekend
bullets: أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي (azuru jaddati) I visit my grandmother
أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي (usa'idu ummi) I help my mother
أَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ (aqra'u l-qur'an) I read the Qur'an
teach.note: Build: فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ (fi nihayati l-usbu') + verb.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: الخَمِيس comes from خَمْسَة (five): the fifth day, Thursday.

practice.q: Say 'At the weekend I help my mother.'
practice.model:
When first: فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ.
Then the verb: أُسَاعِدُ (I help).
Then who: أُمِّي (my mother).

independent.q: Core: Write the seven days in Arabic in order, starting with الأَحَد.
independent.a: الأَحَد، الاِثْنَيْن، الثُّلَاثَاء، الأَرْبِعَاء، الخَمِيس، الجُمُعَة، السَّبْت
independent.model: Teacher writes الأَحَد and الاِثْنَيْن, saying each, and links them to one and two.

independent.q: Extend: Write two sentences about your weekend, starting فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ.
independent.a: For example: فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي. فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ أَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ.

independent.q: Stretch: Which day is your favourite, and why? Write it in English, then the day in Arabic.
independent.a: For example: الجُمُعَة, because I go to Jumu'ah.

exit.q: What is the weekend in Arabic? A) نِهَايَةُ الأُسْبُوعِ B) يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ C) أُسْبُوع
Big question: say one thing you do at the weekend in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي.

lessons.homework: Say the day in Arabic every morning this week, and write one sentence about what you do at the weekend.
lessons.send: SEND: days strip with numbers 1 to 7. EAL: calendar with English and Arabic. Stretch: use 'on Saturday': يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ (yawma s-sabt) + verb.

Portal arabic y4 lesson 3 (days of the week), upgraded
Kitabi: the weekend (CHECK IN KITABI)
Days of the week strip and calendar page (portal worksheet)

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Friends of nature; Layla in the snow; Salem at the zoo
lessons.title: Reading: Salem at the zoo; in, on, under
lessons.bigQuestion: If you could visit one animal at a zoo, which would it be? Where would you find it: in, on or under something?
objectives: To understand a short text about animals and use فِي، عَلَى، تَحْتَ to say where things are
successCriteria: All: say where an animal is with فِي، عَلَى or تَحْتَ
Most: answer أَيْنَ؟ questions about the text
Some: write two sentences about where things are

hook.text: If you could visit one animal at a zoo, which would it be? Where would you find it: in, on or under something?
hook.a: Pupils' own; for example the monkey on the tree: القِرْدُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.

islamicLink.text: Seeing Allah's creation, Muslims say سُبْحَانَ اللهِ (Glory be to Allah).

teach.heading: In, on, under
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Use a pen and a box to show each.

teach.heading: The text
teach.note: Teacher reads twice; pupils read in turn. Our own short text until the Kitabi text is checked (CHECK IN KITABI).

quote.text:
ذَهَبَ سَالِمٌ إِلَى حَدِيقَةِ الحَيَوَانَاتِ.
رَأَى الأَسَدَ فِي القَفَصِ.
القِرْدُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.
السُّلَحْفَاةُ تَحْتَ الصَّخْرَةِ.
قَالَ سَالِمٌ: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ!

teach.heading: Where is it?
teach.note: Questions and answers.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model: Teacher finds the line القِرْدُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ and answers: عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.

independent.q: Where-is-it task on the pupil PDF: three pictures (a cat in a box, a bird on a branch, a ball under a chair). Write a sentence for each, then answer three أَيْنَ؟ questions on the text.
independent.a: القِطَّةُ فِي الصُّنْدُوقِ، العُصْفُورُ عَلَى الغُصْنِ، الكُرَةُ تَحْتَ الكُرْسِيِّ; text answers
independent.model: Teacher writes the first: القِطَّةُ فِي الصُّنْدُوقِ (the cat is in the box).

independent.q: Extend: why did Salem say سُبْحَانَ اللهِ?
independent.a: He was amazed by Allah's creation.

independent.q: Stretch: write where your pen is now.
independent.a: For example: القَلَمُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ

exit.q: 'On' is ...
Back to our ponder: where is your animal?
exit.a: Pupils' own sentence with فِي / عَلَى / تَحْتَ

lessons.homework: Hide a toy at home and ask a family member أَيْنَ ...؟; answer with فِي، عَلَى or تَحْتَ.
lessons.send: SEND: object and box to act out. EAL: preposition cards. Stretch: add بِجَانِبِ (next to).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The weekend; Basem in the village; the little mouse and the lion
lessons.title: Bridge: my school, my family; one and many
lessons.bigQuestion: How does an Arabic word change when there is more than one?
objectives: To understand how Arabic nouns change from singular to plural
successCriteria: All: name four family members in Arabic
Most: say whether a word is مُفْرَد (singular) or جَمْع (plural)
Some: make plurals with ـُونَ (-un) and ـَات (-at)
lessons.crossCurricular: English: singular and plural nouns (book, books; child, children)
lessons.smsc: Moral: kindness to parents and family

hook.text: In English we add 's' for more than one: book, books. Do you think Arabic does the same? How could we find out?
hook.a: Sometimes Arabic adds an ending, and sometimes the inside of the word changes.

islamicLink.text: Allah commands us to be good to our parents (al-Isra 17:23). We start by learning to name our family in the language of the Qur'an.

starter.q: Bismillah. What does هٰذِهِ (hadhihi) mean? A) this (girl word) B) that C) my
Is كِتَاب (kitab) a boy word or a girl word?

teach.heading: My family
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils echo each word. Remind them that -i means my: أُمِّي (ummi) my mother.

teach.heading: My school
teach.note: Point out ة for the female teacher. Ask: boy word or girl word?

teach.heading: Plural with an ending
teach.note: The ة drops off and ـَات is added.

teach.heading: Plural from inside
teach.note: These are learnt one by one, like English mouse and mice.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: What is the plural of مُعَلِّمَة (female teacher)?
check.why: The ة drops and ـَات is added: مُعَلِّمَات.

practice.model:
سَيَّارَة ends in ة.
Take off the ة.
Add ـَات: سَيَّارَات.

independent.q: Core: Copy the table and write the plural: مُعَلِّم، مُعَلِّمَة، سَيَّارَة، كِتَاب.
independent.a: مُعَلِّمُونَ، مُعَلِّمَات، سَيَّارَات، كُتُب
independent.model: Teacher does مُعَلِّم: a man, so add ـُونَ: مُعَلِّمُونَ.

independent.q: Extend: Write three sentences about your family with هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ, e.g. هٰذِهِ أُمِّي.
independent.a: For example: هٰذَا أَبِي. هٰذِهِ أُخْتِي. هٰذَا أَخِي.

independent.q: Stretch: Write: In my school there are teachers: فِي مَدْرَسَتِي مُعَلِّمُونَ وَمُعَلِّمَات.
independent.a: فِي مَدْرَسَتِي مُعَلِّمُونَ وَمُعَلِّمَات

exit.q: What does جَمْع (jam') mean? A) singular B) plural C) family
Big question: how does an Arabic word change for more than one? Give an example.
exit.a: It adds an ending (مُعَلِّمَات) or changes inside (كِتَاب → كُتُب).

lessons.homework: Name five family members in Arabic and make the plural of سَيَّارَة and كِتَاب.
lessons.send: SEND: family word mat with pictures of objects only (no people), e.g. a house. EAL: table with English. Stretch: find the plural of بَيْت (house): بُيُوت (buyut).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The weekend; Basem in the village; the little mouse and the lion
lessons.title: Reading: Basem in the village
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I understand a short Arabic story?
objectives: To understand a short vowelled Arabic text and answer questions about it
successCriteria: All: read the title بَاسِمٌ فِي القَرْيَةِ and five new words
Most: answer three questions on the text
Some: find the verbs in the text
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: villages and towns, and how land is used for farming
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: thanking Allah for animals and the food they give us

hook.text: What would you see, hear and do if you spent a day in a village with farm animals?
hook.a: Fields, cows, hens; we could drink fresh milk and help.

islamicLink.text: Allah reminds us that from the bellies of cattle He gives us pure milk, pleasant for those who drink it (an-Nahl 16:66). Surah al-Baqarah, the longest surah, is named after the cow.

starter.q: Bismillah. Which day is السَّبْت? A) Saturday B) Sunday
Read: القَرْيَة. Sun or moon letter?

teach.heading: New words
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils echo and do an action for each animal (no animal noises needed).

teach.heading: The text

quote.text: يَسْكُنُ جَدُّ بَاسِمٍ فِي قَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ. فِي القَرْيَةِ بَقَرَةٌ وَدَجَاجَةٌ. يَشْرَبُ بَاسِمٌ الحَلِيبَ. يَلْعَبُ بَاسِمٌ فِي الحَقْلِ. القَرْيَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ.
quote.source: Our own short text for 'Basem in the village' (Kitabi version: CHECK IN KITABI)

teach.note: Read slowly, pupils follow with a finger. Then read together. Meaning: Basem's grandfather lives in a small village. In the village there is a cow and a hen. Basem drinks the milk. Basem plays in the field. The village is beautiful.

teach.heading: Who, where, what?
teach.note: Question words help us find answers in a text. Model: أَيْنَ يَسْكُنُ جَدُّ بَاسِمٍ؟ فِي قَرْيَةٍ.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: The text says يَشْرَبُ بَاسِمٌ الحَلِيبَ: Basem drinks the milk.

practice.q: أَيْنَ يَلْعَبُ بَاسِمٌ؟ (Where does Basem play?)
practice.model:
Find the verb يَلْعَبُ in the text.
Read what comes next: فِي الحَقْلِ.
Answer: fi l-haql, in the field.

practice.q: Is the village big or small?
Name the two animals in the village.

independent.q: Core: Copy the text neatly and draw the village (fields, a cow, a hen; no people).
independent.a: Neat copy with a labelled picture
independent.model: Teacher copies the first sentence slowly, showing how ة and ٍ (tanwin) are written.

independent.q: Extend: Answer in Arabic: مَاذَا يَشْرَبُ بَاسِمٌ؟
independent.a: يَشْرَبُ بَاسِمٌ الحَلِيبَ.

independent.q: Stretch: Find the three verbs in the text (they start with يَـ).
independent.a: يَسْكُنُ، يَشْرَبُ، يَلْعَبُ

exit.q: What is قَرْيَة? A) village B) field C) cow
Big question: what helped you understand the story?
exit.a: Knowing the new words first, and using the question words who, where, what.

lessons.homework: Read the text to someone at home and tell them what it means in English.
lessons.send: SEND: text with pictures above key words. EAL: word list beside the text. Stretch: write one more sentence for the story, e.g. القَرْيَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ وَهَادِئَةٌ (beautiful and quiet).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The weekend; Basem in the village; the little mouse and the lion
lessons.title: Verbs in the past and present; unit check
lessons.bigQuestion: How does an Arabic verb show that something has already happened?
objectives: To understand how Arabic verbs change between the past and the present
successCriteria: All: say ذَهَبَ (he went) and يَذْهَبُ (he goes)
Most: match four past verbs with their present forms
Some: retell one sentence of Basem's story in the past
lessons.crossCurricular: English: past and present tense (went, goes)
lessons.smsc: Moral: thinking about what we did yesterday and how we can do better today

hook.text: Yesterday Basem went to the village. Today he goes to school. Which words tell you when it happened?
hook.a: Went (past) and goes (present). Arabic changes the verb too.

islamicLink.text: Allah swears by time in Surah al-'Asr (103:1). Muslims use past, present and future well: we learn from the past and do good today.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is قَرْيَة? A) village B) field

teach.heading: Past and present
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The present adds يَـ (ya-) at the start for he.

teach.heading: More verbs
teach.note: Spot the three root letters in each pair: ش ر ب, ك ت ب, س ك ن.

teach.heading: Basem in the past
bullets: شَرِبَ بَاسِمٌ الحَلِيبَ: Basem drank the milk
teach.note: Change يَشْرَبُ in the story to شَرِبَ. The meaning moves to the past.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which verb is in the past?
check.why: كَتَبَ (he wrote) has no يَـ at the start: it is past.

teach.heading: Unit check: our words
teach.note: Quick review before the check task.

practice.q: Change to the past: يَلْعَبُ بَاسِمٌ فِي الحَقْلِ.
practice.model:
Find the verb: يَلْعَبُ.
Take off the يَـ and use the past form: لَعِبَ.
Keep the rest: لَعِبَ بَاسِمٌ فِي الحَقْلِ.

independent.q: Core (unit check, portal response box or paper): 1) Match past and present: ذَهَبَ، كَتَبَ، شَرِبَ with يَشْرَبُ، يَذْهَبُ، يَكْتُبُ. 2) Write the weekend days. 3) Translate قَرْيَة and بَقَرَة.
independent.a: 1) ذَهَبَ يَذْهَبُ؛ كَتَبَ يَكْتُبُ؛ شَرِبَ يَشْرَبُ 2) السَّبْت وَالأَحَد 3) village, cow
independent.model: Teacher matches ذَهَبَ with يَذْهَبُ: same letters ذ ه ب, one with يَـ.

independent.q: Extend: Write two sentences about Basem in the past.
independent.a: For example: ذَهَبَ بَاسِمٌ إِلَى القَرْيَةِ. شَرِبَ بَاسِمٌ الحَلِيبَ.

independent.q: Stretch: Write what Basem does now and what he did yesterday with one verb.
independent.a: For example: يَكْتُبُ بَاسِمٌ الآنَ. كَتَبَ بَاسِمٌ أَمْسِ.

exit.q: What does ذَهَبَ mean? A) he went B) he goes C) he plays
Big question: how does an Arabic verb show it already happened?
exit.a: The past form has no يَـ at the start, e.g. ذَهَبَ not يَذْهَبُ.

lessons.homework: Write three things you did yesterday, using ذَهَبْتُ (I went), شَرِبْتُ (I drank) or لَعِبْتُ (I played), with help from your verb table.
lessons.send: SEND: verb cards in two colours (past, present). EAL: actions for each verb. Stretch: 'I went': ذَهَبْتُ (dhahabtu), adding ـتُ.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Friends of nature; Layla in the snow; Salem at the zoo
lessons.title: Friends of nature: plants and animals
lessons.bigQuestion: If nature could talk, what do you think it would ask people to do?
objectives: To understand and use Arabic words for plants and animals in nature
successCriteria: All: name five nature words
Most: describe a nature word with هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ
Some: say a sentence about where an animal lives
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: plants and animals in habitats

hook.text: If nature could talk, what do you think it would ask people to do?
hook.a: Look after it: Allah made us caretakers of the earth.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'It is He who has made you successors upon the earth' (al-An'am 6:165): we look after His creation.

teach.heading: Nature words
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Show photos.

teach.heading: This is ...
bullets: هٰذِهِ شَجَرَةٌ: this is a tree
هٰذَا نَهْرٌ: this is a river
teach.note: Remind: girl words with ة take هٰذِهِ.

teach.heading: Friends of nature
bullets: We do not harm trees and animals
Allah made the earth for us to look after

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model: Teacher: زَهْرَة ends in ة, so هٰذِهِ. Together: هٰذِهِ زَهْرَةٌ.

independent.q: Nature poster on the pupil PDF: label six pictures (tree, flower, bird, river, mountain, sun) and write two هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ sentences.
independent.a: Correct labels; for example هٰذِهِ شَجَرَةٌ، هٰذَا عُصْفُورٌ
independent.model: Teacher labels the tree and writes هٰذِهِ شَجَرَةٌ.

independent.q: Extend: say 'the bird is on the tree'.
independent.a: العُصْفُورُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ

independent.q: Stretch: say one way to be a friend of nature in Arabic or English.
independent.a: For example: I water the flowers: أَسْقِي الزُّهُورَ

exit.q: زَهْرَة is ...
Back to our ponder: what would nature ask us?

lessons.homework: Go outside or look out of the window and name three nature things in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: picture word mat. EAL: هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ cards. Stretch: write three sentences.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Friends of nature; Layla in the snow; Salem at the zoo
lessons.title: Reading: Layla in the snow (لَيْلَى فِي الثَّلْجِ)
lessons.bigQuestion: What is the first thing you would do if you woke up and saw snow?
objectives: To understand a short Arabic text about a snowy day and answer questions on it
successCriteria: All: read the title and find three snow words
Most: answer three questions about the text
Some: retell the text in two sentences

hook.text: What is the first thing you would do if you woke up and saw snow?
hook.a: Pupils' own; Layla puts on her coat and goes out to play.

teach.heading: New words
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Pre-teach with photos. Our own short text until the Kitabi text is checked (CHECK IN KITABI).

teach.heading: The text
teach.note: Teacher reads twice; pupils follow with a finger, then read in turn.

quote.text:
خَرَجَتْ لَيْلَى إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ.
الثَّلْجُ أَبْيَضُ، وَالجَوُّ بَارِدٌ.
لَبِسَتْ لَيْلَى مِعْطَفًا وَقُفَّازَيْنِ.
لَعِبَتْ لَيْلَى فِي الثَّلْجِ مَعَ أَخِيهَا.
ثُمَّ رَجَعَتْ إِلَى البَيْتِ وَشَرِبَتْ حَلِيبًا سَاخِنًا.

teach.heading: Meaning
bullets: Layla went out to the garden
The snow is white; the weather is cold
She wore a coat and gloves; then drank hot milk

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Where did Layla go? Answer in Arabic.
practice.model: Teacher finds the line: خَرَجَتْ لَيْلَى إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ. Answer: إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ.

independent.q: Reading questions on the pupil PDF: five questions (two in Arabic, three in English), then underline every verb that ends in ـَتْ (she did).
independent.a: Garden; white; coat and gloves; with her brother; hot milk. Verbs: خَرَجَتْ، لَبِسَتْ، لَعِبَتْ، رَجَعَتْ، شَرِبَتْ
independent.model: Teacher answers question 1 and underlines خَرَجَتْ.

independent.q: Extend: what does ـَتْ at the end of a verb tell us?
independent.a: A girl (she) did it, in the past.

independent.q: Stretch: retell in two Arabic sentences.
independent.a: For example: خَرَجَتْ لَيْلَى. لَعِبَتْ فِي الثَّلْجِ.

exit.q: ثَلْج is ...
Back to our ponder: what would you do first in snow?
exit.a: Pupils' own; for example: أَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفًا (I put on a coat)

lessons.homework: Read the text to a family member and tell them what it means.
lessons.send: SEND: text with pictures above key words. EAL: glossary strip. Stretch: change Layla to a boy and change the verbs (خَرَجَ، لَبِسَ ...).
resources: Slides
Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)
Pupil PDF worksheet: Layla in the snow text and questions

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Friends of nature; Layla in the snow; Salem at the zoo
lessons.title: The imperative: giving instructions
lessons.bigQuestion: The first word revealed of the Qur'an was an instruction. Do you know it?
objectives: To understand how to give simple instructions in Arabic using the imperative
successCriteria: All: follow five Arabic instructions
Most: give three instructions to a partner
Some: change an instruction for a girl (ـِي)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the value of reading and learning

keywords.def: the imperative: an order or instruction

hook.text: The first word revealed of the Qur'an was an instruction. Do you know it?

islamicLink.text: The first word revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was اِقْرَأْ: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (al-'Alaq 96:1).

starter.q: Say 'the monkey is on the tree'.

teach.heading: Classroom instructions
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Teacher says, pupils act (Simon-says style, spoken only).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Give your partner three instructions in Arabic (breakout pair).
practice.model: Teacher gives three to the class: قُمْ! (pupils stand) اُنْظُرْ! (pupils look) اِجْلِسْ! (pupils sit).

independent.q: Instruction cards on the pupil PDF: match six instructions to pictures (pen, book, chair, ear, eye, arrow up), then write a three-step instruction for making wudu-ready: 'اِغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ' etc.
independent.a: Matches correct; e.g. اِغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ، اِغْسِلْ وَجْهَكَ، اِجْلِسْ
independent.model: Teacher matches اُكْتُبْ to the pen picture.

independent.q: Extend: what does اِغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ mean?
independent.a: Wash your hands.

independent.q: Stretch: turn three instructions into girl forms.
independent.a: اُكْتُبِي، اِقْرَئِي، اِجْلِسِي

exit.q: قُمْ means ...
Back to our ponder: what was the first word revealed?

lessons.homework: Give a family member five Arabic instructions and see if they can follow them (teach them first!).
lessons.send: SEND: action pictures. EAL: instruction cards. Stretch: three girl-form instructions.
resources: Slides
Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)
Pupil PDF worksheet: instruction cards

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Friends of nature; Layla in the snow; Salem at the zoo
lessons.title: Complete sentences: the nominal sentence
lessons.bigQuestion: 'The tree tall.' Arabic says it like this, with no 'is'. Is that strange or clever?
objectives: To understand how an Arabic sentence can start with a noun (mubtada') and tell us about it (khabar)
successCriteria: All: say a sentence like الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
Most: find the mubtada' and the khabar
Some: build three nominal sentences with correct girl and boy forms
lessons.crossCurricular: English: subject and predicate in a sentence

keywords.def: a sentence that starts with a noun
the subject: what we talk about
the news: what we say about it

hook.text: 'The tree tall.' Arabic says it like this, with no 'is'. Is that strange or clever?
hook.a: Clever: Arabic doesn't need 'is': الشَّجَرَةُ طَوِيلَةٌ.

teach.heading: Two parts
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Examples
bullets: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ: the weather is cold
الشَّجَرَةُ طَوِيلَةٌ: the tree is tall
النَّهْرُ كَبِيرٌ: the river is big
teach.note: Girl noun (ة) → girl khabar (ة).

teach.heading: Build it
teach.note: Pupils choose the right khabar.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: In الثَّلْجُ أَبْيَضُ, the khabar is ...
check.why: The khabar tells us about the snow: white.

practice.q: Make a sentence: the flower (الزَّهْرَة) + beautiful (جَمِيل).
practice.model: Teacher: الزَّهْرَة is a girl word (ة), so جَمِيل becomes جَمِيلَة. Sentence: الزَّهْرَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ.

practice.q: The mubtada' in القِرْدُ صَغِيرٌ is ...

independent.q: Sentence builder on the pupil PDF: join six nouns to the right khabar (big, small, cold, beautiful, tall, white), then write three sentences and underline the mubtada' in one colour and the khabar in another.
independent.a: For example: البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ، الشَّجَرَةُ طَوِيلَةٌ، الثَّلْجُ أَبْيَضُ
independent.model: Teacher writes البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ and underlines البَيْتُ (mubtada') and كَبِيرٌ (khabar).

independent.q: Extend: write a sentence about the weather today.
independent.a: For example: الجَوُّ حَارٌّ / بَارِدٌ

independent.q: Stretch: why does the khabar have no ال?
independent.a: Because it is the new information about the mubtada'.

exit.q: مُبْتَدَأ is ...
Back to our ponder: strange or clever?

lessons.homework: Write three nominal sentences about things in your home.
lessons.send: SEND: two-colour sentence cards. EAL: noun and adjective banks. Stretch: four sentences with girl and boy forms correct.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Friends of nature; Layla in the snow; Salem at the zoo
lessons.title: Review and check: nature, reading and sentences
lessons.bigQuestion: Which Arabic sentence from this half term could you teach a younger brother or sister?
objectives: To understand how much I remember from this half term and show it in speaking and writing
successCriteria: All: name five nature and zoo words
Most: read a short text and answer two questions
Some: write three correct sentences (where, instruction, nominal)

hook.text: Which Arabic sentence from this half term could you teach a younger brother or sister?
hook.a: Pupils' own, for example القِرْدُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.

teach.heading: What we learned
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Read and check
teach.note: New short text (our own).

quote.text:
الحَدِيقَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ.
العُصْفُورُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.
الزَّهْرَةُ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ.
quote.source: Our own text for the Year 4 check

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model: Teacher finds the line and answers: عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.

independent.q: Oral and written check on the pupil PDF: label six words, answer three questions on the text, write one instruction and one nominal sentence; then say two sentences to the camera.
independent.a: Labels, answers and sentences from the unit
independent.model: Teacher does the first label and the first spoken sentence.

independent.q: Extend: write a sentence with an instruction and a place: اِجْلِسْ عَلَى الكُرْسِيِّ.
independent.a: Sit on the chair.

independent.q: Stretch: write two sentences about your garden or park.
independent.a: For example: الشَّجَرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ. العُصْفُورُ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.

exit.q: Which part will you practise?
Back to our ponder: which sentence would you teach?

lessons.homework: Practise the words you found hardest for five minutes a day.
lessons.send: SEND: picture-supported check. EAL: word mat. Stretch: three sentences from memory.
